channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: The far right is 'missing the butt' of the GTA VI joke: It's them!
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 20: We look at reactions to the historic summit in Shenzhen between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Also, COP31 heads into its final stretch, but fossil fuels have vanished from the draft deal. Plus, the Guardian features a long read on "Power Slapping". Finally, we look at a different kind of hobby: "Grand Theft Auto VI" is finally out.

item.title: Critics are calling what brand-new release a masterpiece? The quiz knows
item.description: Plus: Are you up to date on your James Bond news? If so, you'll get at least one question right.

item.title: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: '/> New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths. (Image credit: Nicky Quamina-Woo)

item.title: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin to announce presidential bid
item.description: France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, is expected to formally launch his presidential campaign Friday. But while De Villepin’s opposition to Israel’s Gaza campaign and assured analysis of international affairs has caught the eyes of younger voters, it remains to be seen if he can persuade them to cast a ballot for him.

item.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
item.description: A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences. (Image credit: Stefan Rousseau)

item.title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal
item.description: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars.

item.title: Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
item.description: Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions with a show of cross-border solidarity.

item.title: Households stockpiling 'emergency items' boosts retail sales
item.description: Shoppers appear to be heeding government warnings to stock-up on essentials amid a surprise leap in retail sales.

item.title: Live: Several killed, dozens wounded in Russian attacks that damaged two Kyiv bridges
item.description: Russian attacks on Ukraine killed eight people and woulded 28, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi ​said on ‌Friday. The fresh wave of missile and drone attacks – which also damaged two bridges in Kyiv – came after Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo officially enter FIFA presidential race
item.description: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

item.title: Czechs protest en masse against 'concentration of power in one hand' and growing control over media
item.description: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says.

item.title: Trump-Putin-Xi meeting updates: Schumer calls trip a 'historical embarrassment'
item.description: Trump participated on Thursday in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: DOJ dropping Alaska midterms Senate certification lawsuit, saying case is 'moot'
item.description: The Justice Department is giving up on its controversial lawsuit that sought to potentially block the certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate race.

item.title: Man accused of killing British woman sent knife with her blood on to friend
item.description: A man accused of murdering a British woman he met on a fetish website sent a knife with her blood on it to a friend, a US court has heard.

item.title: EU and UK set to sign deals on trade, energy, youth mobility at Brussels summit
item.description: The UK and the EU are poised to agree new deals on trade, energy and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels on Friday, as part of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's bid to reset ties with the bloc. Burnham – who has said he hopes to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime – argues the deals will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.

item.title: White House fires national cyber director over widespread outages
item.description: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The departure comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over its response to the outages, which officials say were unrelated incidents.

item.title: Army postpones plan to detonate nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide until Monday
item.description: Two rapid controlled detonations scheduled to take place at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Friday have been postponed by three days.

item.title: WATCH: Motorcyclist survives after fiery crash with Tesla
item.description: A motorcyclist walked away from a fiery crash on an L.A. freeway after suddenly being cut off by a Tesla in the left lane.

item.title: PM Sanchez admits 'mistakes' in key debate ahead of Spain's election
item.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far-right Vox party in a position to enter government.

item.title: Trump China trip: Iran and Ukraine not in 'peace declaration' and more takeaways
item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.title: Trump pardons late baseball great Pete Rose after historic China trip
item.description: On the way back from his Asia trip, President Donald Trump said Thursday he issued a "complete and total pardon" to baseball legend Pete Rose, who died in 2024.

item.title: Met Police can photograph people without consent in facial recognition pilot
item.description: Police officers in London will be able to use their mobile phones to photograph and identify suspects without their consent as part of a new facial recognition pilot.

item.title: Anti-monarchy group hands over 'evidence' on Andrew as it calls for investigation
item.description: An anti-monarchy campaign group says it has given police and the Crown Prosecution Service "evidence" on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

item.title: Voyager 1 spacecraft reaches one light-day milestone
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, which has been traveling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday. Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometers (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency. That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Armed forces in Haiti kill at least 34 gang members to regain control of key corridor
item.description: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.

item.title: Anthropic goes public after blockbuster IPO but fails to revive AI trade
item.description: Anthropic has become the first pure-play AI developer to be publicly traded on the stock market, following a record-setting IPO. The stock opened 34 percent higher, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion, before ending its first day of trading up 17 percent. However, Wall Street indexes closed sharply lower as investors took profits, reflecting underlying market jitters about the AI trade.

item.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
item.description: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left.

item.title: Saudi's tallest skyscraper damaged in Houthi attack
item.description: Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper, the headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck in ​a Houthi attack in the latest in a series of strikes on the Gulf state, Riyadh said.

item.title: Why the U.S. air traffic control system still relies on an 'antique' network
item.description: The FAA says the telecom outage that led to Friday's nationwide ground stop began with an upgrade to fiber-optic cables. Industry experts say the work is long overdue. (Image credit: William Liang)

item.title: England handed suspended away ticket ban for fans' chants during Spain win
item.description: England have been given a suspended away ticket ban by UEFA for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" by their fans during a match with Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

item.title: Thomas Markle fit to stand trial over child abuse images, US court rules
item.description: Thomas Markle is fit to stand trial on charges of possessing child sexual abuse material, a US court has ruled.

item.title: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for doping
item.description: In tonight's edition: Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. Plus Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Dutch and Austrian embassies
item.description: A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged a historic cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. Loud explosions erupted across the Ukraine capital throughout the day as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States held a historic meeting in China that put Russia's President Vladimir Putin in international spotlight. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

item.title: 'We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
item.description: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".

item.title: Iran live updates: Republicans block war powers resolution
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
item.description: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.

item.title: UK conducting offensive cyber ops against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea, says top commander
item.description: The UK is conducting offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea, a top military commander has for the first time revealed.

item.title: Macron urges Ukraine's allies to 'reopen the question' of NATO membership
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for Ukraine's allies to speed up the delivery of urgently needed air defence systems and urged them to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's NATO membership after talks in Berlin aimed at reaffirming European support for Kyiv.

item.title: Trump’s CISA pick rejects Jan. 6 as an 'attack,' won't name 2020 election winner
item.description: Michael LoSapio, President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, says he doesn't consider the Jan_ 6 Capitol insurrection an "attack."

item.title: A president among body bags: Photo ops spark outrage in Colombia
item.description: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos that show him walking among body bags supposedly holding the remains of rebel fighters – a communications strategy that has sparked widespread criticism.

item.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
item.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday. (Image credit: Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

item.title: Three of a kind? Xi hosts Trump and Putin as Ukraine war grinds on
item.description: Gang of three or glorified photo op? Xi Jinping hosting Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Already, our Monday panel rejected attempts to paint the three-way meeting as a new Yalta, as in the 1945 sit-down on the Black Sea that defined the post-war security architecture of Europe.

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting: Trump's recognition of China and Russia as 'peers of the US'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit was significant despite the absence of concrete agreements, according to Cheung. “The significance is seen in the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States,” she explained, adding that “the image of a G3 is very significant.”

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
item.description: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.

item.title: WATCH: Our colleague skips work to play GTA 6
item.description: ABC News associate producer Ben Greenberg took a vacation day to play “Grand Theft Auto VI” and told Kyra Phillips about it live.

item.title: What Obama said to newly elected Democrats after midterm gains
item.description: Former President Barack Obama told Democratic U.S. House members-elect on Wednesday that they should value their ideological diversity even if they have disagreements.

item.title: Xi tells Trump US must do 'the right thing' over Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping used his meeting with President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday to warn against the creation of "turbulence" over the issue of Taiwan.

item.title: Auditors concerned about billions ICE is spending to expand immigration detention
item.description: Federal auditors warn that ICE is spending billions of dollars to expand immigration detention without "determining the cost effectiveness" of new initiatives.

item.title: WATCH: Trump calls Putin, Xi his friends after meeting
item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.title: The 'Magic Six': How to strengthen your marriage in midlife
item.description: How do we maintain healthy romantic relationships as we age? Allison Aubrey and Scott Detrow talk about about the science of healthy, later-in-life relationships. (Image credit: Richard Drury/Getty Images)

item.title: WATCH: 'Kenan and Kel' star has a mission to give back
item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.title: EU reveals it suffered 'AI-powered' cyber attack
item.description: The EU has revealed it suffered a cyber attack powered by AI last month and some of its digital tools are still offline as a result.

item.title: WATCH: Military family gets surprise of a lifetime at 2026 CMAs
item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's Voyager 1 now a light-day away after 1977 launch
item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: Burnham says Europe 'ready to enter negotiations' to help end Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: (L-R) Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin. Pic: Reuters

item.title: WATCH: Man reunited with long-lost cat after 3.5 years
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.

item.title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017. (Image credit: Salahuddin Ahmed)

item.title: UEFA challenges FIFA over access to Infantino World Cup sell-off papers - as presidency rivals revealed
item.description: FIFA has confirmed which candidates will stand in next year's presidential election - as UEFA challenges restrictions placed on documents relating to the World Cup sell-off scandal.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Animal rescuers describe cat rescue after Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: Rescuers are speaking out about the miraculous rescue of Isaac the cat after the deadly building collapse in Brooklyn.

item.title: WATCH: 'Looksmaxxing' influencer Clavicular indicted on rape charges
item.description: Braden Peters is accused of giving alcohol to a teen and sexually assaulting her at his family's Cape Cod home.

item.title: Israeli troops launch ground operation in central Gaza
item.description: Dozens of displaced Palestinians have fled their tents and shelters in central ‌Gaza after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it had left under a ceasefire last year.

item.title: WATCH: Man accused of starting Palisades fire faces retrial
item.description: ABC News legal analyst Brian Buckmire and correspondent Alex Stone explain what prosecutors are arguing differently and the potential sentence if the man is convicted at his federal retrial.

item.title: Hochul demands information from ICE about new immigration tent facility for women
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul is demanding information from ICE and a Virginia-based construction company about a new tent immigration detention facility set to house women.

item.title: William and Kate meet India's PM as they wrap up royal visit
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales met the prime minister of India on Wednesday to discuss trade and bilateral ‌ties at the end of their three-day visit to the country.

item.title: Congressional Republicans push Howard Lutnick, Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia
item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.title: WATCH: Dog sniffs out baby's medical condition
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mother in England whose family dog's actions helped alert her that her baby boy had a congenital heart condition.

item.title: WATCH: Eagles Autism Foundation staff shine on game day
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team's commitment to autism inclusion.
